messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: alternative parameterization for multivariate normal?
parts:
Hi all. Would it make sense to have a paraemterization of the multivariate normal that takes the parameters Sigma^{-1}*mu and Sigma^{-1} (i.e., the so-called natural parameters of the exponential family) rather than mu and Sigma? I'm asking because, in this MC-EP thing I'm playing around with, I find myself doing a lot of inverting matrices and solving linear systems in order to get mu and Sigma to pass in to my prior distribution. It's no big deal in terms of "wall time" (the dimensionality is low), I was just wondering.
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] alternative parameterization for multivariate normal?
parts:
I added a new issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/482

We now have 127 outstanding issues.

We need to prioritize. So far, we've been prioritizing bug
fixes, but maybe that's not the right thing to do?

We currently have two bad bugs outstanding, one that's leaking
memory and one that's crashing Stan when it should be rejecting.
But maybe that's not such a bad thing in the grand scheme of things
compared to adding new distributions?

We've also tried to tighten our dev process to try to prevent
more bugs getting in and keep our design flexible, which means
everything we do now is going much much more slowly than it
used to in the bad-old cowboy days of Stan 1.

- Bob

I maintain that no bugs are so critical that they need to be fixed immediately.
We need to prioritize at weekly meetings, and if a bug is urgent it will be
decided and then tackled there after. We'd be foolish to think we'll ever
tamp down all the bugs, and if devs continue with the current approach
we'll never get to new features.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: alternative parameterization for multivariate normal?
parts:
We already have multi_normal_prec() that takes a precision matrix. But it takes a mu vector rather than Sigma^{-1}*mu.

Ben
